claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page) in the Pulumi docs, linked from the support index.
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes which providers get long-term security updates.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Link target /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists (Provider support policy page).
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes made during an update if an error or failure occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running pulumi up or pulumi preview.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in, enabled via a flag, command, or environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine, and Pulumi native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs without Terraform schemas.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
Pulumi's providers receiving long-term support updates on eligible older versions are: AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
The Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/.

A Pulumi provider LTS release contains High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or direct dependencies and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers are compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at, unless otherwise prompted via security fixes.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When major N+1 ships, it becomes the new N and the old N becomes the new LTS major; the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day, regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS provider releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a provider automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major version is recommended.
N is the latest released major version: if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1, and v1 and earlier are end of life; older majors than the LTS version receive no patches.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life versions (N-2 and older) are not supported and will not receive updates.
The page /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions'.
